palette.role: Permanent woody canopy with the main late-spring flowering display. The reference case for the growth model.

handedness.basis: RHS: "anticlockwise", no viewpoint stated. Viewed from above per Valder (1995); Darwin: "moves against the sun"; Flora of China: "stems twined leftward". All describe a right-handed helix.

attachment.supportNeeds: Strong, continuous leader routes on secondary supports; strain-aware anchors; removable and adjustable ties; access for twice-yearly pruning; clearance for stems that thicken for decades.

wood.basis: RHS: flower buds start to develop in late summer of the previous year. Flora of China: racemes from branchlets of the previous year.

monthsUK.basis: Months read from the RHS season wording (spring = Mar-May, summer = Jun-Aug, autumn = Sep-Nov, winter = Dec-Feb; early, mid and late are the first, second and third month).

flowering.display: Fragrant lilac to mauve racemes to about 30 cm, opening before the leaves.

site.aspect: Full sun or partial shade, preferably south or west facing and sheltered; full sun matters for profuse flowering.
site.soil: Moist but well-drained; avoid prolonged waterlogging.

calendar.note: Summer: cut the whippy green shoots of the current year back to five or six leaves.
Winter: cut the same shoots back to two or three buds.

management.notes: Train and tie in leaders during establishment; once the framework is made, keep to the two-stage spur pruning, trim unruly shoots and inspect ties.

hazards: Mature wood becomes large and heavy; published height says nothing about load.
